requirements.title: Artificial Intelligence concentration within Computer Science BS
Concentration selections; no Breadth of Knowledge reuse
requirements.summary: Complete 12 credit hours from the following if not taken to fulfill Breadth of Knowledge:

requirements.title: Admission to the Program (host major context)
requirements.summary: Formal admission to the major requires a cumulative grade point average of 2.00 (on a 4.00 scale) and departmental approval.

requirements.title: Major Requirements (host major context)
requirements.summary: 62 credit hours with grades of C or better, including at least 40 credit hours at or above 300-level Maximum 6 credit hours of CSC coursework may be substituted for relevant non-CSC coursework with the approval of the program director

requirements.title: Semester credit definition
requirements.summary: AU defines a credit hour through instruction and outside work over a fifteen-week semester or equivalent. Published course and concentration amounts are normalized as semester hours using regulation 1.

requirements.title: Host-major residence and outside-course permission
requirements.summary: Host-major context: at least 18 major credits and 15 upper-level major credits must be in residence. An outside upper-level course within the first 18 major credits requires the teaching-unit chair’s permission. These are major-wide thresholds, not additional concentration course totals.

requirements.title: Host-major grading
requirements.summary: Each major course requires C or better. Students cannot elect pass/fail for major requirements; courses offered only pass/fail are excepted.

requirements.title: What counts as in residence
requirements.summary: AU, Washington Consortium/ROTC, AU Abroad and AU-coordinated instruction count as residence. Transfer, external Permit to Study and examination credit do not.

requirements.title: Domestic outside study and major application
requirements.summary: Post-matriculation domestic study requires good standing, prior academic-unit approval and faculty articulation at an accredited institution. Applying a course to the major requires teaching-unit approval even if already articulated. The ordinary limit is 10 credits or three courses, whichever is greater; grades below 2.00 do not earn transfer credit. Outside grades are excluded from the AU GPA.

requirements.title: Conditional medical Permit to Study
requirements.summary: A medical leave and preapproval are required. Up to two outside courses per term and four courses or 17.5 credits overall (whichever is greater, including other permits) are allowed; units may add restrictions. Residence may be waived. This is an exception path, not an ordinary concentration entitlement.

requirements.title: Non-partner international study
requirements.summary: Good standing and advance academic-unit/AU Abroad approval are required; the opportunity must be unavailable through AU partners. Up to 36 credits may transfer subject to residence, with the amount preapproved and application submitted before the preceding term ends. Outside grades do not enter the AU GPA.

requirements.title: Host-major declaration and changes
requirements.summary: The major is expected to be declared before 60 earned credits with academic-unit approval; units may set higher requirements. Changing a major or school requires good standing and receiving-unit permission.

requirements.title: Conditional second-major university rule
requirements.summary: If pursuing another major, current university regulation 9.6 requires at least 2.50 cumulative GPA and 18 credits unique to each major; units may impose higher requirements. Students choose the graduating academic unit and degree where applicable. This does not turn the AI concentration into a second major.

requirements.title: CAS declaration procedure and published threshold context
requirements.summary: CAS permits declaration after one semester with AU GPA at least 2.0, using its online request reviewed by authorized staff. Meet the appropriate CAS advisor before a second major; declare the first major first. The CAS Second Major section also publishes 2.0, while university regulation 9.6 publishes 2.50. The sources are retained separately; the general CAS statement is not treated as an exception to the university rule. Some majors have higher GPA/gateway requirements.
